Security policy

Source: SECURITY.md

Supported versions

Security fixes are made on the 0.18.x line (0.18.0 and later 0.18.x releases) and on the latest CRAN release once there is one. Older versions are not patched.

Version Supported
0.18.x yes
0.10.x to 0.17.x best effort
0.3.x to 0.9.x best effort (never released publicly)
< 0.3 no

Reporting a vulnerability

Please do not open a public GitHub issue for a security problem. Email the maintainer privately instead:

max.moldovan@adelaide.edu.au

Use a subject line such as [flexyBayes SECURITY] <one-line description>.

The maintainer will:

  1. Acknowledge the report within 7 days.
  2. Reply in substance within 30 days, with a fix plan or an explanation of why the issue will not be fixed.
  3. Coordinate the fix and any public disclosure, normally with a 90-day embargo from the first acknowledgement.

If you have had no response within these times, open a public GitHub issue at https://github.com/AAGI-AUS/flexyBayes/issues, without sensitive details, asking whether the report arrived.

Scope

flexyBayes is written in R and generates INLA and Stan model code. Areas of likely security interest are:

  • input that can reach eval() or parse() during formula parsing or code generation
  • file paths passed to R CMD INSTALL or to vignette build scripts
  • user-supplied numeric data in code generation.

Problems in INLA, brms or Stan themselves should be reported to those projects.
